prompt.context_jp: 事務室に差し込む昼下がりの光____、テーブルに置かれた小さな包みを白く縁取っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 事務室に差し込む昼下がりの光____、テーブルに置かれた小さな包みを白く縁取っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this scene-setting narration.

feedback.correct_en: This opens the chapter by introducing the afternoon light as new, descriptive information — a classic scene-setting が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 光 as an already-established topic, but here the narrator is painting a fresh image for the first time.

prompt.context_jp: ハナが社長に問い返す場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私のプライドを なんで社長____守るんですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Hana uses to challenge Motomi.

feedback.correct_en: Hana is challenging who exactly would be doing the protecting — 社長が identifies the subject with focus ('why would YOU of all people').
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 社長 a casual topic, losing the pointed, accusing nuance Hana carries here.

contrast_examples.jp: なんであなたがやるの？
contrast_examples.en: Why are YOU the one doing it?

prompt.context_jp: 元美が告白めいた一言をこぼす場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「正直 言うと 私____ハナさんに関心があります」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits a reflective self-statement.

feedback.correct_en: 元美 is setting herself up as the topic to share her own feelings — 私は is the natural self-introductory frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would exhaustively claim 'I am the one' interested, sounding oddly competitive instead of confessional.

contrast_examples.en: I'M the one interested. (as opposed to others)

prompt.context_jp: 元美が自分の母について語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私の母____自分を愛せない人なんだって」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle to introduce 母 as the subject of this realization.

feedback.correct_en: 元美 is stating a defining truth about her mother as the topic — 私の母は frames the characterization.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as new identifying information ('it's my mother who...'), which doesn't fit this reflective realization.

contrast_examples.en: My mother is a kind person. (topic + description)

prompt.context_jp: 元美が自分の決意を語る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私____男のためには生きない」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 元美's declaration about herself.

feedback.correct_en: She's declaring her own stance as the topic — 私は contrasts her with others who might live for men.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would exhaustively identify the subject, which doesn't match the self-defining tone.

contrast_examples.en: I (for my part) won't give up.
I'll be the one to decide.

prompt.context_jp: ラベンダーについての説明。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「上のラベンダー____ ただの飾りなので…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the lavender as the described item.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is explaining what the lavender IS — a classic topic-description structure with は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like identifying which thing is decoration, out of place in a general description.

prompt.context_jp: 元美が疑問を口にする場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いえ 問題____ありません」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 問題 in this negative response.

feedback.correct_en: In negation, は often marks the thing being denied — '(as for) problems, there aren't any.' This matches the contrastive reassurance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 問題がありません is grammatical but 問題はありません better fits an answer that pushes back on an assumed topic (Hana just asked if there's a problem).

prompt.context_jp: ハナが車を降りて景色を見る描写。
prompt.prompt_jp: 眼下には斜面いっぱいのブドウ畑____広がり…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this descriptive landscape.

feedback.correct_en: The vineyard appears as fresh descriptive information in the scene — new-information が is standard for 'X spread out.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the vineyard a pre-established topic, but here it's being introduced visually for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: That sea is blue. (topic already set)

prompt.context_jp: 寛がハナの正体に気づく瞬間。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あれ ハナさん____だったんだ 健二先生の」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this 'oh, it was YOU' realization.

feedback.correct_en: Realization/identification sentences ('oh, it was you!') exhaustively identify the subject with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make Hana a mere topic, missing the 'you were the one!' discovery nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 航が二人の様子を観察して言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ハナさんって いっつも 社長____見てますもん…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Kou uses to say Hana only looks at the president.

feedback.correct_en: The original line is 社長だけ見てます — the restrictive 'only' adverb だけ fits the meaning 'she looks only at the boss.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が or は would lose the 'only' meaning that makes Kou's observation pointed.

prompt.context_jp: 壮亮が携帯の待ち受けを見せる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この写真 ____ お父さんの作品です」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for introducing the photo as topic.

feedback.correct_en: He's identifying what the (already visible) photo IS — classic 'A は B です' topic+description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively point out which photo is dad's work, which doesn't match showing one specific wallpaper.

prompt.context_jp: 元美がハナに言い返す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私____ いつ避けましたか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Motomi uses to deny avoiding Hana.

feedback.correct_en: 元美 pushes back by focusing on herself as subject — 私が emphasizes 'when did I (of all people) avoid you?'
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は would soften it into a general topic question; the dialogue needs the sharper 'I' focus.

contrast_examples.en: When did I ever say that?

prompt.context_jp: ハナが自分について語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私みたいな人____ もう… やっぱり独りが似合います」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 私みたいな人.

feedback.correct_en: ハナ is characterizing her kind of person as topic, implicitly contrasting with others — 私みたいな人は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify who suits being alone, sounding odd in this reflective self-assessment.

contrast_examples.jp: 私みたいな人は向いてない。
contrast_examples.en: People like me aren't cut out for it.
HE is the one suited for it.

prompt.context_jp: 元美がハナを気遣った理由を説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「それは… ____だと思って」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits '(I thought it was) ___'.

feedback.correct_en: かわいそう ('pitiable, sorry for') fits Motomi's protective excuse — Hana later repeats '私が…かわいそう？'
feedback.incorrect_en: かわいい (cute) and かっこいい (cool) don't match the sympathy context.

prompt.context_jp: 元美が片思いの状況を描写する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「片思いがダメになる 一歩____なんですから」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression for 'one step before.'

feedback.correct_en: 一歩手前 is the set phrase for 'one step away/short of' — fits 'on the verge of heartbreak.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 後ろ (behind) and 向こう (beyond) don't form this idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 元美が母の過去を語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「____ごとに 自殺未遂とかして 相手の気を引こうとしてた」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'at every incident.'

feedback.correct_en: 事あるごとに is a fixed phrase meaning 'at every turn / whenever something happens.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 時ある/物ある aren't valid set phrases in this slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 事あるごとに注意する。

prompt.context_jp: ハナが寛に謝る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「2回… ____ました 寛さんのこと」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'stood (someone) up.'

feedback.correct_en: すっぽかす means 'to stand (someone) up / blow off an appointment' — exactly what Hana is confessing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見逃す = overlook; 追い越す = overtake. Neither fits apologizing for missing a date.

prompt.context_jp: 寛がハナと社長について冗談めかして言う。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'you make a good couple.'

feedback.correct_en: お似合い = 'well-matched / suits each other,' the standard compliment for a couple.
feedback.incorrect_en: お疲れ (tired/greeting) and お世話 (care) don't form this compliment.

contrast_examples.en: The two of you make a good couple.

prompt.context_jp: ワイン試飲でおかわりを頼んだのを見て。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「飲み放題の居酒屋____ないんだから」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the right form after a noun to say 'it isn't X.'

feedback.correct_en: 居酒屋じゃないんだから = 'because it's not an izakaya' — じゃ is the colloquial copula negation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が and を can't form a negative copula with ない here.

prompt.context_jp: 元美がハナを評する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「心を込めて仕事をする ____な従業員で」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective meaning 'sincere/earnest.'

feedback.correct_en: 誠実 = 'sincere, earnest' — fits an employee who 'puts their heart into their work.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 確実 = certain/reliable (about facts); 切実 = urgent/dire. Neither captures sincerity of character.

prompt.context_jp: ハナが壮亮を突き放すように言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「普通のカップルみたいなのが ほんと嫌だし ____」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning '(it's a) bother/nuisance.'

feedback.correct_en: 迷惑 is the sharp 'you're bothering me / a nuisance' word Hana uses to push him away.
feedback.incorrect_en: 面倒 (bothersome task) and 退屈 (boring) exist but don't match the original line nor the emotional force here.

prompt.context_jp: 元美がコートを返してもらう場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural coming from Motomi in this casual-but-blunt moment?

choices.text: 泊まりで長野なの 頂戴 コート
泊まりで長野なんです コートを頂戴いたします

feedback.correct_en: The clipped, casual の + the inverted 頂戴 コート matches Motomi's blunt, deflecting style with Hana here.
feedback.incorrect_en: The overly polite version mixes humble 頂戴いたします with 頂戴 awkwardly and clashes with the private boss-employee moment.

contrast_examples.jp: ペンをいただけますか。

prompt.context_jp: 元美がドアの前で振り返って言う。
prompt.prompt_en: Which option sounds more natural for a casual 'see you by chance again' farewell?

choices.text: また偶然 会いましょう
また偶然 会うことになりましょう

feedback.correct_en: また偶然会いましょう is a natural, light send-off. The actual line uses this crisp form.
feedback.incorrect_en: 会うことになりましょう sounds stilted and semantically odd — 'become to meet' doesn't pair with 偶然.

contrast_examples.jp: また会うことになるね。

prompt.context_jp: 寛が片思いについて語る。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'nobody would be stuck on unrequited love'?

choices.text: 片思いする人なんて 一人もいないと思いますよ
片思いする人なんか 一つもいないと思いますよ

feedback.correct_en: People are counted with 一人, not 一つ. 一人もいない is the natural 'not a single person.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 一つもいない misuses an inanimate counter for people and sounds wrong.

prompt.context_jp: 元美が二人きりの時間を作ってあげる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as a casual nudge between adults?

choices.text: せっかくだからさ 2人で ゆっくりしてきたら？
せっかくだからさ 2人で ゆっくりしてくるのはいかがでしょうか？

feedback.correct_en: 〜してきたら？ is the natural casual suggestion — matches the friendly nudge Motomi gives.
feedback.incorrect_en: いかがでしょうか is overly formal and clashes with the casual さ/2人で register.

contrast_examples.en: Why don't you go take a break?

contrast_examples.jp: 休憩されてはいかがでしょうか。
contrast_examples.en: Would you care to take a break? (formal)
